 How N.C. Will Resolve Races That Are Still Too Close to Call 
 County election boards will meet this week to perform machine recounts in contested races, including multiple state legislative and congressional battles. 
 by 
 Bryan Anderson 
 November 17, 2026 November 17, 2026

 Election Day ended two weeks ago, but several races remain too close to call.
 Ten state legislative and congressional candidates who were within one percentage point of winning their races had until this week to request recounts. Half of them conceded, while the other half filed for recounts.
 Over the next week, county election officials across the state will meet for those machine recounts. The State Board of Elections has advised counties to complete all tabulations by Monday, November 23. The board intends to certify results at its November 24 meeting.

 U.S. House District 5: Democrat Chuck Hubbard leads Republican U.S. Rep. Virginia Foxx by 331 votes, or 0.12 percentage points. An updated vote tally should be available by Monday, when Guilford County is likely to complete its tabulations.
 NC House District 20: Democrat Tim Merrick leads Republican Dane Scalise by 77 votes, or 0.18 points. State officials hadn’t posted the New Hanover County Board of Elections’ meeting schedule as of Tuesday afternoon, so it isn’t immediately clear when the recount will end.
 Senate District 24: Republican state Sen. Danny Britt leads Democratic challenger Catina Hamm by 224 votes, or 0.4 points. Scotland County completed its recount on Monday night, and the other two counties in the district should be done by Thursday.
 NC House District 62: Democrat Shelly Headen leads Republican incumbent John Blust by 267 votes, or 0.62 points. The Guilford County Board of Elections is scheduled to begin its recount Thursday morning and expects the process to take two or three days.
 U.S. House District 10: Republican U.S. Rep. Pat Harrigan leads Democratic challenger Ashley Bell by 2,510 votes, or 0.85 points. Lincoln County reported updated results on Monday night. An updated vote tally should be available by Friday, when Forsyth County is scheduled to complete its tabulations.
 If the trailing candidate decides to press forward after a machine recount, they’ll have 24 hours to request a partial hand count in a random sample of 3% of Election Day precincts, early voting sites, or both. That would begin within two business days of the request. Depending on the results, a third recount could then take place, involving a full hand count of all ballots cast.

 Given the margins of the leading candidates, it’s unlikely any of the outcomes of legislative or congressional races will change. In recounts in both the 2020 and 2024 state Supreme Court contests, a handful of votes shifted in races separated by several hundred votes.
